subject: Archaeology
title: Rongorongo of Easter Island
description: Learn Rongorongo of Easter Island in one minute.

hook.text: Easter Island has a writing system that no other Pacific culture developed. Only 26 surviving tablets exist.

buildup.text: Rongorongo glyphs show humans, animals, plants, and geometric shapes carved into wooden boards in a boustrophedon.

discovery.text: Missionaries in the 1860s recorded that only a few chiefs could read the script. Slave raids killed most of them.

twist.text: Some scholars believe Rongorongo was independently invented — one of only a handful of times writing was created from scratch.

climax.text: With so few tablets and no living readers, decipherment may never be possible.

punchline.text: A tiny island invented writing independently.

quiz.question: Why can't Rongorongo be deciphered?
options: The wooden tablets have decayed beyond recognition
Only 26 tablets survive, and slave raids killed the last people who could read it
It is written in invisible ink that only appears under certain light

details.summary: Rongorongo is an undeciphered script found on wooden tablets from Easter Island. If proven to be true writing invented independently, it would be one of only a handful of cases of independent writing invention in human history.
details.whyItMatters: Independent invention of writing is extraordinarily rare. If Rongorongo is genuine indigenous writing, Easter Island joins Mesopotamia, China, and Mesoamerica in the exclusive group of civilizations that invented writing independently.
takeaways: An undeciphered script on wooden tablets from Easter Island
May represent independently invented writing — extremely rare
Only about two dozen tablets survive worldwide

faq.question: Why are there so few Rongorongo tablets?
faq.answer: Christian missionaries in the 1860s encouraged islanders to burn objects associated with pagan practices. Most tablets were destroyed. Only about two dozen survive in museums worldwide. The loss of tablets and of anyone who could read them makes decipherment nearly impossible.

faq.question: Could Rongorongo have been inspired by European contact?
faq.answer: Some scholars suggest that seeing Spanish writing in 1770 inspired islanders to create their own. However, the script's complexity and the sophistication of its symbols argue for longer development. The debate remains unresolved because so few examples survive.
